claim: Prompt injection via a PR title hijacked Anthropic's Claude Code Security Review, Google's Gemini CLI Action, and GitHub's Copilot agent to leak API keys and tokens, yet vendors paid small bounties and published no CVEs.
quote: crafted a PR title containing a prompt injection payload. Claude executed the embedded commands... Anthropic: $100 bounty; severity rating upgraded from 9.3 to 9.4... None of the three vendors assigned CVEs or published advisories

claim: The 'Comment and Control' attack class writes a payload into a PR title, issue body, or comment; the agent treats it as trusted and exfiltrates credentials back through GitHub's own APIs, bypassing env-var filtering and secret scanning.
quote: a malicious payload is written into a GitHub pull request title, issue body, or comment, and when an AI coding agent processes that content, it treats the attacker's instructions as trusted and executes them — typically exfiltrating API keys and access tokens back through GitHub itself

claim: GitGuardian found 28.6M new secrets in public GitHub commits in 2025 (a 34% YoY jump), and commits co-authored by Claude Code leaked secrets at roughly double the baseline rate, showing agent-accelerated code outpaces credential governance.
quote: 28,649,024 new secrets exposed in public GitHub commits across 2025, a 34% year-over-year increase... Commits co-authored by Claude Code leaked secrets at roughly double the baseline rate... Integration velocity can increase by 10x, but credential governance doesn't scale at the same rate

claim: AI review systematically misses business logic, architecture, edge cases, and context-dependent security because it does not know what the application is supposed to do; false-positive alert fatigue erodes trust faster than missed issues.
quote: AI lacks understanding of your product's unique requirements... Design patterns, system boundaries, and long-term scalability implications require experience and context AI doesn't possess... Context-dependent security issues often slip through because AI doesn't know what your application is supposed to do... Alert fatigue...erodes trust faster than missed issues

claim: AI review fatigue leads developers to rubber-stamp suggestions and within a month skim or ignore comments entirely; performance degrades on PRs over 500 lines, and self-review bias arises when the same model writes and reviews code.
quote: developers start rubber-stamping AI suggestions without critical evaluation... After a month, they are skimming or ignoring AI comments entirely... performance deteriorates on changes exceeding 500 lines... when the same AI model generates code and reviews it, there's risk of self-review bias

claim: CodeRabbit reviews aggressively but at roughly 50.5% precision, meaning about half of its comments point to real issues and the other half are noise, cluttering PRs.
quote: 50.5% precision means roughly half of CodeRabbit's comments point to real issues. The other half are suggestions that may not be actionable... reviews aggressively... Produces more comments, some of which are noise

claim: Practitioners report AI introduces security headaches reviews miss: hardcoded secrets, credentials exposed in logs/workflows, unsafe curl|bash suggestions, and untraceable agent actions using shared API keys.
quote: Secrets leaking left and right — AI suggesting code that hardcodes stuff or exposes creds in logs/workflows... when an agent makes a call using a shared API key and something goes wrong, there is no way to prove what it was authorized to do... secrets passed as shell args, pasted into logs, broad credentials reused across runs
